evidence.detail: The Add Archetype form's <select name='parent'> has a default <option value=''>[Select]</option>, so submitting without choosing a parent sends parent='' (empty string)
Condition is 'request.form.get("parent") is not None' — an empty string is not None, so the branch is entered
cast_int() is int(cast(str, param)); int('') raises ValueError causing a 500
If name is provided but parent is empty, cast_int(request.form.get('parent')) is reached and raises ValueError

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/controllers/admin.py post_archetypes(): inside the 'parent is not None' block (line 112), guard against an empty parent string before calling cast_int — e.g. check 'if not request.form.get("parent"):' and return edit_archetypes() with an error. This mirrors the existing pattern in post_rules() (line 137-138). May require adding an 'add_errors' parameter to the EditArchetypes view (decksite/views/edit_archetypes.py) and a corresponding display in editarchetypes.mustache. Total: ~15-25 lines across 3 files.
triage.notes: The silent no-op path (empty parent AND empty name) also silently does nothing rather than showing 'please select a parent' — fixing the 500 case naturally also fixes this UX gap.
